summary: Installed AIDE on node1 (RHEL 10) and established a content-aware integrity baseline for /etc. The default AIDE config only monitored permissions/ownership for /etc broadly (PERMS rule, no content hash) — strengthened it to NORMAL (adds sha512 content hashing) so file content edits are detected, not just metadata changes. Initialized the baseline database, verified a clean check, proved detection works by modifying /etc/motd and observing AIDE flag it, then reverted the test change and re-baselined to a clean state. Added a systemd service+timer for daily automated checks/reporting. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the AIDE database, timer, and detection capability all survived and function correctly post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed aide package via dnf on node1
Inspected /etc/aide.conf and found the blanket /etc rule used PERMS only (no content hash)
Edited /etc/aide.conf: changed '/etc PERMS' to '/etc NORMAL' to add sha512 content hashing; backed up original to /etc/aide.conf.orig.bak
Ran aide --init and activated the database (aide.db.new.gz -> aide.db.gz)
Verified clean baseline via aide --check (no differences)
Validated detection: appended a line to /etc/motd, aide --check flagged it (exit=4, 'f > ...H....: /etc/motd')
Reverted the test change to /etc/motd and re-verified clean baseline
Created and enabled systemd aide-check.service + aide-check.timer (daily) for ongoing automated integrity checks/reporting
Ran aide --update to fold the new systemd unit files into the baseline, activated updated database, verified clean check
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health (clean AIDE check, timer active/enabled)
Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed (7223d5b7... -> 8c8e9aed...), proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart: AIDE database md5sum unchanged, timer active/enabled, aide --check clean
Re-validated detection post-restart (motd edit flagged), then reverted and confirmed final clean baseline state
